drafted_from: tool:list-the-longest-still-holds-of-my-video's row in tools/check-a-videos-motion-against-a-reference/tool-rows.json, do-work/list-holds.mjs, read-data/measure-motion.mjs and test/list-holds.test.mjs; the answers were observed by running the command on an ffmpeg test clip
start_here: Say to your AI: "List the three longest places where clips/draft.mp4 holds still, with the second each one starts, up to its end card at 5 seconds." It reads the video on your computer and gives each hold as its length and start second, longest first.
no_lists_because: It names no list: it reads one video file on your computer and prints the holds it found.
instructions: 1. On your computer, clone the Workshop checkout and run brew install ffmpeg (this brings ffprobe). Run everything from the root of the checkout.
2. If you just ran tool:check-a-videos-motion-against-a-reference, take its still_threshold and the end card second; passing them makes the list match the holds the check counted.

3. Say to your AI: "Where does my video hold still longest?" It reads the row with tools:list {tool}, then runs: node tools/check-a-videos-motion-against-a-reference/do-work/list-holds.mjs --video clips/draft.mp4 [--seconds S] [--still LEVEL] [--top N]

4. Read the last line: {"result": {video, seconds, still_threshold, holds, text}}. holds is longest first, each {seconds: length, at: start second}; top defaults to 12. Open the video at each start second and fix the hold.

worked_examples.title: Two holds in a 7 second clip, then only the first 3.5 seconds at the check's still level
worked_examples.ask: Where does clips/two-holds.mp4 hold still longest?
worked_examples.given: Run locally from the Workshop checkout after tools:list: node tools/check-a-videos-motion-against-a-reference/do-work/list-holds.mjs --video clips/two-holds.mp4. clips/two-holds.mp4 is made as in tools/check-a-videos-motion-against-a-reference/test/list-holds.test.mjs: a moving pattern for 2 seconds, grey for 1, moving for 1, grey for 2, moving for 1 (7 seconds). Read from do-work/list-holds.mjs and observed by running it; adding --seconds 3.5 --still 1.5 answers {"result":{"video":"clips/two-holds.mp4","seconds":3.5,"still_threshold":1.5,"holds":[{"seconds":0.93,"at":2}],"text":"0.93s@2.00"}}.
